title: Principality of algebraic equivariant fusion for Hopf algebras with bijective antipode, principal comodule algebras and two jointly surjective C-star quotient maps
author: Ludwik Dabrowski; Tom Hadfield; Piotr M. Hajac
source_title: Equivariant Join and Fusion of Noncommutative Algebras
difficulty_reason: The construction combines the original strong connection with an antipode-controlled trivial connection through two square-root cutoff elements obtained by C-star functional calculus. The proof verifies both quotient boundary constraints and the canonical splitting, then derives Hopf-Galois bijectivity and equivariant projectivity from a nonunital connection criterion; it covers fusion without a pullback join decomposition.
source_version: Official SIGMA 11 (2015) article 082, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2015.082; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: Complete Lemma3.3 nonunital connection criterion, the fusion comodule restriction Lemma5.2 and full Theorem5.3 square-root connection construction read. H has bijective antipode, P is principal as both Hopf-Galois and equivariantly projective, C is a unital complex C-star algebra, J1/J2 are C-star ideals and the direct sum of canonical quotient maps is surjective. The tensor products in Section5 are algebraic; the analytic C-star fusion completion is not selected. Every boundary corestriction and splitting is explicitly displayed, and bicolinearity follows from the given input connection. No example, ordinary join specialization or conjectural nontriviality statement is counted.

statement_scope: Full Theorem5.3 in the algebraic Section5 setting: equivariant fusion P fusion_delta,pi H is principal under the standing bijective-antipode and principal-right-H-comodule assumptions, with unital C-star algebra C and jointly surjective quotient map C->C/J1 directsum C/J2. No claim that arbitrary non-surjective maps, generic diagonal coactions or a C-star completion satisfy this theorem.
